Rumors suggest Apple will unveil new products on October 13, and based on the timing of past October events, here's a timeline of when Apple might announce the event date.

Will Apple hold an October event?

Apple's September events have historically followed a fairly regular schedule, but October events are far less predictable, with both the dates and the timing of advance announcements proving difficult to pin down.

Since 2010, Apple has held only ten October events, the most recent being the Halloween-themed "Scary Fast" event on the evening of October 30, 2023.

Here's a look at how far in advance Apple has announced each October event since 2010:

Year Event Announcement date Event date 2023 “Scary Fast” Tuesday, October 24 Monday, October 30 2021 “Unleashed” Tuesday, October 12 Monday, October 18 2020 “Hi, Speed” Tuesday, October 6 Tuesday, October 13 2018 “There’s more in the making” Thursday, October 18 Tuesday, October 30 2016 “Hello again” Wednesday, October 19 Thursday, October 27 2014 “It’s been way too long” Wednesday, October 8 Thursday, October 16 2013 “We still have a lot to cover” Tuesday, October 15 Tuesday, October 22 2012 “We’ve got a little more to show you” Tuesday, October 16 Tuesday, October 23 2011 “Let’s talk iPhone” Tuesday, September 27 Tuesday, October 4 2010 “Back to the Mac” Wednesday, October 13 Wednesday, October 20

That said, Bloomberg previously reported that Apple is planning to launch the long-rumored smart home hub, a next-generation HomePod mini, and an Apple TV 4K with brand-new Siri AI features on Tuesday, October 13, though it did not specify whether Apple would hold an event to announce these products.

If true, Apple could announce the event date as early as next Monday (October 5), but no later than Wednesday, October 7.

It's worth noting that Apple is also expected to reveal an iPad mini with an OLED display, an all-new iMac, and several new MacBook Pro models (including a version with a touchscreen) in 2026. Whether these products will be announced at the same event, a separate event, or via press release remains unclear.

Looking back, in October 2024, Apple unveiled new Mac products via press releases over three consecutive days, while in October 2025, it launched the M5 chip alongside new iPad Pro, MacBook Pro, and Apple Vision Pro models without holding an event.

By comparison, Apple has only held one event in November — the "One More Thing" event in November 2020, which introduced the first Macs powered by the M1 Apple Silicon chip.

Of course, 2020 was a rather unusual year for Apple's event schedule. Due to the COVID-19 pandemic disrupting the normal timeline, the company held a rare WWDC at the end of June, followed by separate events in September and October.

What new products do you think Apple will announce at the rumored October event? Let us know in the comments.
